title: Tony Hills Newsletters
key_points: Pinterest now detects 'same-ish' pins, so changing only a title or slightly changing a design is no longer enough — pins need different keywords, user situations, hooks, visuals, and boards
Newer pins can now rank in 2-4 weeks instead of months, especially for newer accounts or newer blog posts, so the old advice to start Christmas pins in July/August is outdated
A knitting audience searches months ahead for Christmas because handmade gifts take time, while a recipe audience searches closer to the holiday, often after Thanksgiving

Pinterest Trends workflow: set Trend type to Top monthly trends, choose Interest category, set End date to past dates like 11/30/2023, scan for seasonal keywords, then repeat changing end date month by month through July/August, September 30, October 31, November 30, December 31
Interest Explorer finds long-tail official Pinterest interests that may not appear in Trends but can help with home feed visibility

Ranking factors for a strong pin: target keyword in pin title, target keyword in pin description, relevant annotated interests in description, visually appealing image, relevant text overlay if top-ranking pins use text, correct user intent, and timely/relevant topic
When studying top pins, look at: number of saves, date pinned, annotated interests, pin style (image-only, text overlay, collage), adjectives used, main colors, description style and keywords

PinClicks Keyword Explorer example for 'day hike' showed keyword scores: rainy day hike outfit (200), multi day hike packing list (151), day hike food (149), what to pack for a day hike (131), day hike lunch ideas (113), day hike checklist (108), day hike snacks (106)
The PDF rejected 'day hike lunch ideas' because many newer pins already targeted it, but chose 'day hike first aid kit' because top results were older and not specifically targeting that phrase
TOBI pins (text on background image) was identified as the top-performing style for the day hike first aid kit keyword

Keyword annotations extracted from the top pin included: Camping Supplies, Camping And Hiking, Camping, Backpacking Tips, Backpacking, Hiking First Aid Kit, Backpacking For Beginners, Hiking Essentials, Hiking Backpack
When Interest Explorer returned no results for 'day hike first aid kit', broadening to 'first aid kit' revealed official interests: hiking first aid kit and hiking first aid kit checklist
Keywords should appear closer to the beginning of the blog post where possible
Pins should be pinned to boards with names matching official Pinterest interests — example given was pinning to boards named 'Day Hikes' and 'First Aid Kits'

Annotations are hidden keyword phrases Pinterest associates with pins using signals from: pin title, pin description, URL, board name, board description, page title, page description, and objects detected in the image
Annotations are visible when logged out of Pinterest but hidden when logged in — PinClicks can show annotations for top 25 ranking pins including occurrence frequency
Pinterest now evaluates pin diversity across topics (interest keywords), intent (shopping, planning, saving), and style (visual look, design, aesthetic)

Keyword Planner cluster report example for 'cottagecore' showed 10 clusters with 279 keywords, including: Cottagecore Living Room (score 25, volume 62,384), pink cottagecore aesthetic living room (score 9), cottagecore big living room (score 8), cottagecore living room mobile home (score 2), cottagecore living room with kids (score 2), cottagecore living room with tv (score 2)
Strategy is to turn keyword clusters into separate blog posts and pins for different situations instead of one generic post
summary:
The newsletters present a Pinterest strategy centered on creating keyword-led, visually diverse, intent-specific pins rather than generic or repetitive ones. Pinterest now detects 'same-ish' pins, so merely changing titles or making slight design variations no longer works. The approach requires targeting different keywords, user situations, hooks, visuals, and boards for each pin.

The first section covers seasonal Pinterest traffic, noting that newer pins can now rank in 2-4 weeks rather than months, changing the old advice about starting holiday pins in July/August. Timing depends on niche: knitting audiences search months ahead for handmade Christmas gifts, while recipe audiences search closer to holidays, often after Thanksgiving. The PDF provides specific Pinterest Trends instructions: set Trend type to Top monthly trends, choose Interest category (example: Home Decor), set End date to past dates like 11/30/2023, scan for seasonal keywords, then repeat month by month. Example keywords shown include thanksgiving table settings, christmas decor ideas for living room, and home inspo. Interest Explorer is recommended for finding long-tail official Pinterest interests not in Trends.

The PinClicks workflow section demonstrates a complete SOP using 'day hikes' as the niche example. In Keyword Explorer, searching 'day hike' returned scored keywords including rainy day hike outfit (200), multi day hike packing list (151), and day hike food (149). The PDF rejected 'day hike lunch ideas' because newer pins were already targeting it, but selected 'day hike first aid kit' because top results were older and non-specific. Top pins were analyzed, revealing TOBI (text on background image) as the winning style. Annotations extracted from the top-ranking pin included Camping Supplies, Backpacking Tips, Hiking First Aid Kit, Hiking Essentials, and Backpacking For Beginners. Interest Explorer returned 'hiking first aid kit' and 'hiking first aid kit checklist' as official interests after broadening the search.

The annotations section explains these are hidden keyword phrases Pinterest assigns to pins using signals from pin title, description, URL, board names, page title, page description, and image object detection. Annotations appear when logged out but are hidden when logged in. PinClicks shows annotations for top 25 ranking pins with occurrence data. The practical use is choosing the top 3-5 most relevant annotations for new pins.

The final section addresses Pinterest's home feed changes aimed at reducing repetitive and low-quality content. Pinterest now evaluates diversity across topics (interest keywords), intent (shopping, planning, saving), and style (visual look, aesthetic). Pins using the same background image with slightly different text may now be seen as the same pin. A Keyword Planner screenshot showed a cottagecore cluster report with 10 clusters and 279 keywords, including specific variations like cottagecore living room with kids (score 2) and pink cottagecore aesthetic living room (score 9). The strategy is to create separate blog posts and pins for these different situations rather than one generic post.
